messages:
maya: quick question — we need to settle span naming + attributes for LLM requests. proposals: namespace prefix, token fields, kvcache, route id, but worried about cardinality and PII.
adrian: +1 to `llm.` prefix. prefer snake_case keys, e.g. `llm.operation`, `llm.model.id`, `llm.input_tokens`, `llm.output_tokens`, `llm.kvcache_hit`.
jules: snake_case is fine but watch high-cardinality values like full model hash or route names. we should hash route/customer ids and keep raw for internal-only exporters.
samir: also: don't emit prompt text or user message. add `redwood.sensitive=true` if request contained user content so exporters can drop it. for cache keys: emit `llm.kvcache_bucket` (coarse) and `llm.kvcache_hit` boolean.
kevin: exporters: we should route telemetry with `exporter.allow_sensitive` flag. long-term retention = drop high-cardinality attributes (model.revision, route hash), keep aggregated metrics (token histograms). sample code:
```json
{"span.name":"llm.generate","llm.operation":"generate","llm.model.id":"gptx-7b","llm.model.revision":"r3","llm.input_tokens":45,"llm.output_tokens":128,"llm.kvcache_hit":true,"redwood.route_hash":"sha256:..."}
```
maya: That looks good. one more UX point: span.name should be generic like `llm.request` or `llm.generate`? i vote `llm.request` with `llm.operation` for types (generate, embed, rerank) so we can group by span.name easily across ops.
adrian: agree. also add `llm.batch_size` if batched, and `llm.quantized=true` for quant config.
jules: propose retention rules: high-cardinality attrs expire after 7d in observability, low-cardinality kept 90d. sensitive=true attr forces 24h TTL.
kevin: add telemetry docs checklist to PR template and a linter rule in CI that flags new llm.* keys without a registry entry.
tracebot: CI check — telemetry-schema: new keys found: none. all good :white_check_mark:
maya: ok i'll draft RFC with examples and export routing rules. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
